purpose: Primary-table verified observations for Doogh and Iranian breads. Not consumed by enrichment, publisher, meal aggregation, or nutrition UI.

sources.title: Evaluation and Comparison the Physicochemical Properties Pasteurized Kefir and Doogh
sources.sampleDescription: Three pasteurized Doogh products A/B/C and three kefir products A/B/C purchased from Tehran stores; Doogh sample count n=3.
sources.methods: pH meter; titration for acidity; referenced standard methods for moisture, salt, protein and ash; cited method for calcium and phosphorus.
sources.basis: Table 1 reports percentages but does not clearly define an as-consumed per-100g standard basis.
limitations: Calcium and phosphorus percentages conflict with total ash and need independent verification

sources.title: Evaluation of Salt, Sodium, and Potassium Intake Through Bread Consumption in Chaharmahal and Bakhtiari Province
sources.sampleDescription: 451 traditional bread samples collected in 2016 in Chaharmahal and Bakhtiari; Sangak n=25, Barbari n=35, Lavash n=29.
sources.methods: Potentiometric salt analysis and flame photometry for sodium and potassium.
sources.basis: mg/100g bread as labelled in Table 1; table does not explicitly resolve wet/as-sampled versus dry-matter basis; moisture is separately reported.
limitations: Modest sample sizes for three target bread types

sources.title: Evaluation of nutrients in bread: a systematic review
limitations: Secondary source; Table 4 misattributes 451-sample survey to Tabibian et al. [48], whose reference is an unrelated vitamin D fortified-bread paper. Cite Aalipour 2019 as the primary source.
